Marcy’s full pension after 40 years would be  

\[
P = \$50{,}000 .
\]

After she has worked 20 years, each additional year gives her an extra 5 % of the pension’s value.  
The amount added each year is  

\[
0.05 \times P = 0.05 \times 50{,}000 = \$2{,}500 .
\]

She quits after 30 years, i.e., 10 years beyond the 20‑year mark.  
Thus the total percentage of the pension she has earned is  

\[
10 \times 5\% = 50\% .
\]

Her annual pension is therefore 50 % of the full pension:

\[
\text{Annual pension} = 0.50 \times 50{,}000 = \boxed{\$25{,}000}.
\]
